The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and the Department of War signed a safety agreement for the southern border and completed a safety assessment of a high-energy laser counter-drone system, validating that the technology does not pose undue risk to passenger aircraft [FAA and Department of War Sign Landmark Safety Agreement Protecting the Southern Border](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-and-dow-sign-landmark-safety-agreement-protect-southern-border). This action clears a regulatory hurdle for deploying advanced counter-unmanned aircraft systems (C-UAS) in critical national security zones. The FAA simultaneously advanced its broader strategy to integrate advanced air mobility (AAM) into the National Airspace System by unveiling eight selections for pilot program testing of next-generation eVTOL and AAM aircraft [FAA Unveils Eight Selections for Pilot Program Testing Next-Generation Aircraft](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/future-aviation-here-trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-and-faa-unveil-eight). These demonstrations will validate operations across personal travel, regional transport, cargo logistics, and emergency medicine, marking a significant step toward commercial viability.

In related AAM developments, BETA Technologies and United Therapeutics completed a flight test of organ medical-transport capabilities in an eVTOL aircraft moving cargo from Virginia to Maryland [FAA Marks Major eVTOL Milestone as Organ Medical Transport Flies Virginia to Maryland](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-announces-major-milestone-evtol-technology-use). The FAA marked this milestone as a major step in the eVTOL Integration Pilot Program toward real-world medical and emergency use. Additionally, the Department of Transportation and FAA broke ground on a new advanced air mobility research facility in Oklahoma City to support testing, training, and integration of eVTOL and other advanced aircraft [DOT and FAA Break Ground on New Facility to Support Advanced Air Mobility Research](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/dot-and-faa-break-ground-new-facility-support-advanced-air-mobility-research).

The FAA also took a pivotal step toward enabling civil supersonic flight over the continental United States, citing advances in technology that will make quieter, safer supersonic commercial operations feasible over populated areas [FAA Takes Pivotal Step Toward Enabling Civil Supersonic Flight Over the U.S.](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-supersonic-flight-coming-us). In the autonomous vehicle sector, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) is moving to let driverless trucks use cab-mounted warning beacons in place of the traditional hazard warning triangle, modernizing federal safety requirements for autonomous commercial vehicles [FMCSA Permits Driverless Trucks to Swap Warning Triangles for Cab-Mounted Beacons](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiuAFBVV95cUxNQlVRTk1zNHRWQnNXcm1RV2Y2Q1VIR212OXJxaUVVb1oxQWxpUjY1WVhiMHhMZzVrSml2TGdVQVN5a3czLUpmNDZZUEY4cEkxTUFmMktBSUppQUNxNkpRcUYwa1VEdmF3NzROR0J2dmdXdGM4QS0ySjg1dTZONFdqOEtIc2NndGU2cjNtWTVlNDlTX3VoZXkwelRYdU43dlk2WGFpRy13NU0wSXA5LUctZDM5ZTlDRjFr?oc=5).

Infrastructure investments continue to support these technological shifts. The FAA is investing $84.4 million in Airport Improvement Program grants across Texas, North Carolina, and Wyoming to strengthen and modernize regional airports [FAA Invests $84.4 Million in Airport Improvements in Texas, North Carolina, and Wyoming](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/trumps-transportation-secretary-sean-p-duffy-announces-844-million-airport-improvements). Furthermore, the agency awarded $12 million to 19 companies for drone research and testing projects intended to expand drone operations safely in the National Airspace System [FAA Awards $12 Million for Drone Research and Safe Airspace Integration](https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/faa-funds-drone-research-support-safe-integration).
